column1: # clues.tsv for ft_memset -- pedagogic hints only, each a question. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a hint fires when ANY of its cases fails)
man memset: "fills the first n bytes of the memory area pointed to by s". Which byte is the first one your function writes, which is the last, and what does it do when n is 0?
What does memset return (man memset, RETURN VALUE) -- and is that the pointer your function hands back on every path?
c arrives as an int, and memory holds bytes. For 0, 128, 233 or 255, which byte ends up in memory -- how wide is what your function writes through, and does any test in it depend on the value of c?
If the small rows pass and this one does not, does anything in your function depend on n being small -- the type of a counter, a buffer of a fixed size?
